record.paper_title: Some open problems in dynamical systems
record.original_question: Fix α ∈ T^n satisfying a Diophantine condition. Let C^∞_0(T^n) be the space of smooth real-valued functions on T^n with Haar integral 0, and for ϕ in this space define the exact symplectic diffeomorphism F_ϕ on T^*T^n ≅ T^n × R^n by F_ϕ(θ,r) = (θ + r, r + ∂ϕ/∂θ(θ + r)). Let U_α be the set of ϕ for which F_ϕ leaves invariant a smooth torus T_{α,ϕ}, given as the graph of a smooth map ψ : T^n → R^n, and such that F_ϕ restricted to that torus is smoothly conjugate to the translation R_α : θ ↦ θ + α. Is the boundary ∂U_α, viewed inside C^∞(T^n), a locally flat C^k submanifold for some k ≥ 0?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n\geq 1$ and fix $\alpha\in\mathbb{T}^n=\mathbb{R}^n/\mathbb{Z}^n$ satisfying a Diophantine condition: there exist $\gamma>0$ and $\tau\geq n-1$ such that $|k\cdot\alpha-m|\geq \gamma|k|^{-\tau}$ for all $k\in\mathbb{Z}^n\setminus\{0\}$ and $m\in\mathbb{Z}$. Let $C^\infty_0(\mathbb{T}^n)$ denote the Fréchet space of smooth real-valued functions on $\mathbb{T}^n$ with zero Haar integral. For $\varphi\in C^\infty_0(\mathbb{T}^n)$, define the exact symplectic diffeomorphism
$$F_\varphi : T^*\mathbb{T}^n\cong \mathbb{T}^n\times\mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{T}^n\times\mathbb{R}^n,\qquad F_\varphi(\theta,r)=\bigl(\theta+r,\; r+\tfrac{\partial\varphi}{\partial\theta}(\theta+r)\bigr).$$
Let $U_\alpha\subset C^\infty_0(\mathbb{T}^n)$ be the set of $\varphi$ for which $F_\varphi$ admits a smooth invariant torus $T_{\alpha,\varphi}$ given as the graph of a smooth map $\psi:\mathbb{T}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n$, such that the restriction $F_\varphi|_{T_{\alpha,\varphi}}$ is smoothly conjugate to the translation $R_\alpha:\theta\mapsto\theta+\alpha$. Endow $C^\infty_0(\mathbb{T}^n)$ with its usual $C^\infty$ topology.

Question: Is the boundary $\partial U_\alpha$ of $U_\alpha$ in $C^\infty_0(\mathbb{T}^n)$ a locally flat $C^k$-submanifold for some integer $k\geq 0$?
artifact.status_search_result: No published resolution of this question about the regularity/local flatness of the boundary of the set of perturbations admitting a Diophantine KAM torus was located. The question is widely cited as an open problem in KAM theory, and searches on KAM literature and recent surveys on linearization and invariant tori reveal no announced solution.

status_evidence.title: Introduction to KAM theory with a view to celestial mechanics (Féjoz)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of KAM theory discussing the set of parameters with invariant tori, without resolving the local-flatness question for the boundary.
status_evidence.claim: Recent KAM surveys do not record a resolution of the boundary-regularity question.

status_evidence.title: On the linearization of analytic diffeomorphisms of the torus
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on linearization of torus diffeomorphisms; does not announce a resolution of the boundary local-flatness problem.
status_evidence.claim: Recent linearization literature does not claim a resolution.
